title: The diffusive component of intestinal glucose absorption is mediated by the glucose-induced recruitment of GLUT2 to the brush-border membrane
funder: Not read: the Portland Press PDF returned HTTP 403, the PubMed Central copy is PDF-only behind a browser check, and the PubMed and Crossref records list no funder.
result: Read in the abstract. In perfused rat jejunum in vivo, phloretin, a GLUT2 inhibitor, strongly inhibited absorption; brush-border GLUT2 rose about 2-fold when luminal glucose was raised from 0 to 100 mM. The phloretin-sensitive component was carrier-mediated and co-operative (n = 1.6, half-maximal at 56 mM glucose), and paracellular flow was negligible; the SGLT1-mediated component was half-maximal at 27 mM. The authors conclude that GLUT2-mediated facilitated diffusion across the brush-border membrane is the principal route of glucose absorption, up to 3-fold greater than that by SGLT1.
